title: Scientific synthesis
description: The final scientific result of an investigation. Every field is an integrated conclusion drawn from artifacts produced in the sandbox, never from memory.

objective.description: The scientific question this investigation answered, in the scientist's terms.

summary.description: A scientific conclusion a biologist can read on its own: what was established, how strongly, and what it means. Not a worklog of what was run.

findings.description: One entry per distinct scientific claim. Order by importance.

title.description: The claim as a short scientific statement, e.g. 'Ser160 is the catalytic nucleophile', not a step name.

statement.description: What the evidence shows, stating which parts are KNOWN deposited records and which are CALCULATED in this sandbox.

confidence.description: HIGH only when independent lines of evidence agree. Never assert experimental validation.

evidence_files.description: Basenames of attached artifacts that support this claim.

implications.description: What this claim means for the scientist's decisions.

agreements.description: Points where independent lines of evidence converge.

disagreements.description: Counter-evidence and conflicts between sources or calculations. Report these, never omit them.

knowledge_gaps.description: What remains unresolved and could not be settled with the available data or tools.

recommended_next_steps.description: Concrete next experiments or calculations, each tied to the evidence and uncertainty motivating it.

limitations.description: Method limitations that bound the conclusions, e.g. rigid-receptor docking, short simulation, small homolog set.
